column1: # Feed registry — the sources this project watches for NEW information.
# One row per feed. Columns are TAB separated:
#   key                stable short name, used in state and reports
#   url                the feed URL
#   cap                OBJ ORG MONEY EVENT TECH POLICY
#   cadence_claimed    what the PUBLISHER says, verbatim enough to check,
#                      or "unstated". Documentation only — nothing reads it
#   stale_after_hours  OUR threshold. The only number the check uses
#   window             when the publisher actually rebuilds, or blank for
#                      always. "Mon-Fri 06:00-22:00 America/New_York".
#                      Time OUTSIDE the window does not count as silence
#   verified           yes|no — has this URL been fetched and parsed BY US
#   verified_on        ISO date of that measurement, or blank
#   basis              why this feed is in the list. >40 chars
# WHY cadence_claimed AND stale_after_hours ARE TWO COLUMNS
# The first version of this file had one, cadence_minutes, and the code
# multiplied it by six. Both halves were wrong, and the first real run
# proved it in one line: at 23:34 ET on Monday 2026-10-12 it called both
# SEC XBRL feeds LATE because they were last built at 21:50 ET. The SEC
# publishes them "every ten minutes Monday through Friday, 6am - 10pm
# EST" — 21:50 is the LAST TEN-MINUTE SLOT BEFORE CLOSE. The feeds were
# flawless; the check had kept the number from that sentence and thrown
# away the conditions, then scored the publisher against a multiplier
# this project invented. A threshold now has a visible author. See
# HOLIDAYS ARE NOT MODELLED. The window knows about weekends and nights,
# not about Columbus Day. The thresholds below are therefore set so that
# ONE closed weekday (16 in-window hours) cannot trigger LATE on its
# own, and two consecutive ones can. That is a deliberate trade: one
# missed alarm over a long federal weekend, rather than a false alarm
# every holiday, which is the kind of noise that gets a check ignored.
# VERIFIED 2026-10-13 from the conda env: eight of eight fetched,
# parsed, and offered conditional-GET headers. 12 requests, 3 hosts.
# ONE ROW REFUSED, AND WHY IT IS A COMMENT RATHER THAN A verified=no:
# fed_register_sec returned HTTP 200 with 10,595 bytes of
# `text/html; charset=utf-8` whose <title> is
#     Federal Register :: Request Access
# carrying a CSRF token and a CSP nonce. That is not a broken URL or a
# changed pattern — it is an access gate, and the page's own title says
# what it wants: automated clients should request access rather than
# fetch. The standing instruction is to violate no site's policy, so
# the response is to STOP REQUESTING IT, not to look more like a
# browser. The row is commented out so neither --verify nor --poll can
# send another request to a door that has been closed, and the reason
# travels with it.
# Their sanctioned route for programs is the Federal Register JSON API
# at api.federalregister.gov. It is NOT an RSS feed and does not belong
# in this file; it belongs in docs/API_USAGE_POLICY.md once somebody
# reads its documented terms from the publisher's own developer page.
# Unread, so unwritten (AD-112).
# REFUSED 2026-10-13: Federal Register, SEC agency id 466. Access-gated.
# https://www.federalregister.gov/articles/search.rss?conditions%5Bagency_ids%5D%5B%5D=466
# SOURCES CHECKED AND NOT ADDED, 2026-10-14. Recorded so nobody looks
# twice, because "I could not find a feed" and "there is no feed" are
# different findings and only one of them is worth writing down:
#   CelesTrak      NO FEED EXISTS. celestrak.org links no RSS or Atom;
#                  it says "Follow @TSKelso and @CelesTrak on Bluesky".
#                  It also says "Please be sure to adhere to our usage
#                  policy when retrieving any CelesTrak data", and this
#                  project already reads CelesTrak elsewhere, so the
#                  answer is not to synthesise a feed from a social
#                  account.
#   FCC            Daily Digest is EMAIL ONLY - "You can have the Digest
#                  emailed to you daily" - and www.fcc.gov/rss returned
#                  a client error. No feed URL to add. The Digest is the
#                  publisher's own route and a person can subscribe to
#                  it; a mailbox is not this module's business.
#   ESA            esa.int/Services/RSS_Feeds says the list "is
#                  available on the right" and the sidebar did not
#                  render to the fetcher. The feeds exist; their URLs
#                  were not READ. Open one in a browser, then --check.
# Nothing above is written in as a guess. That is the whole rule here.
key
sec_press
column9: SEC press releases. Enforcement and rule changes that move a filer's disclosure obligations, which is upstream of every number sec_edgar.py reads. Carries no lastBuildDate, so it reports UNDATED and the threshold is nominal.

column1: sec_litigation
column9: SEC litigation releases. A filer under enforcement is a filer whose reported figures may be restated, and a restatement is a competing claim rather than a correction. Also carries no lastBuildDate.

column1: sec_xbrl_usgaap
column9: Up to 200 latest filings with US-GAAP or IFRS tagged statements, each carrying edgar:cikNumber and edgar:assignedSic. The arrival signal for sec_edgar.py: tells us a new 10-K exists without polling 16 filers.

column1: sec_xbrl_all
column9: All XBRL filings, up to 200. Broader than the US-GAAP feed and the cheapest way to notice a space filer we never seeded, because every item carries its SIC.

column1: nasa_news
column9: NASA news releases. Mission milestones, award announcements and programme changes. Measured rebuilding same-day on 10-13, so a week of silence is genuinely odd for this one.

column1: nasa_technology
column9: NASA technology news, adjacent to the TechPort TRL data already ingested. Measured 10 days between builds on 10-13, which is normal for a topical feed and is why the threshold is 30 days rather than a week.

column1: nasa_jpl
column9: JPL centre news, the highest spacecraft-per-release rate of any NASA centre feed. Measured 4 days between builds, so it gets the topical threshold rather than the news one.

column1: nasa_all
column9: NASA recently-published content, all of it. Kept as the fallback if the topical feeds prove too narrow; expected to be noisy, and its build time tracked nasa_news exactly on 10-13.

column1: arxiv_space
column9: arXiv instrumentation-and-methods plus space-physics preprints, one combined feed so it costs one request. Upstream of the TechPort TRL data: a sensor or propulsion method appears here years before it has a TRL. Terms read at info.arxiv.org/help/api/tou.html 2026-10-14 - 1 req/3s across all machines, which is why MIN_INTERVAL_S is 3.0. 72h because arXiv does not announce every night and this project has not read which nights, so no window is claimed.
